results.title: Crosswalk Mapping. Many cybersecurity and regulatory… | by Athira K B | Medium
results.content: # Crosswalk Mapping. Organizations can simplify their compliance procedures by recognizing and utilizing the common control requirements across several frameworks. Organizations can take a more integrated and strategic approach to compliance by using crosswalk mapping to methodically find equivalencies across several frameworks. ## Crosswalk Mapping. Crosswalk mapping involves aligning cybersecurity and data privacy frameworks, standards, and regulations to pinpoint areas of overlap and differences. Crosswalk mapping aids teams in visualizing the connections between frameworks, enabling them to comprehend how requirements correspond, identify gaps, and streamline efforts across various regulatory demands. By leveraging crosswalk mapping, organizations can more effectively navigate the complex regulatory landscape, reduce compliance fatigue, and strengthen their overall security and privacy programs. Implementing crosswalk mapping provides strategic advantages across compliance, security, and operational domains:. 1. **Enhanced Compliance:** By aligning multiple frameworks, organizations can more easily identify and fulfill overlapping regulatory and control requirements, improving overall compliance posture. 2. **Reduced Redundancy:** Mapping reveals where frameworks require similar or identical controls, enabling teams to implement a single control that satisfies multiple obligations and avoids duplicative effort. 5. **Eliminate Duplicate Work:** Crosswalk mapping significantly reduces the manual burden of conducting separate assessments for each framework by enabling unified control implementation and evidence reuse. 6. **Improved Audit Readiness:** By centralizing control mapping and aligning evidence across frameworks, organizations can respond more efficiently to audits, assessments, and regulatory inquiries — saving time and reducing stress. Starting with release 2024.1, the SCF now leverages the Set Theory Relationship Mapping (STRM for crosswalk mapping, since STRM is generally well-suited to evaluate cybersecurity and data privacy laws, regulations and frameworks. You can either use pre-existing crosswalk mappings that meet the requirements of your company or make customized mappings that are suited to your particular control system as a compliance specialist. If you decide to create your own crosswalk mapping, think about analyzing the textual content of your reference and target frameworks using AI and Natural Language Processing (NLP) approaches. By combining AI-driven insights with expert judgment, organizations can create reliable, efficient, and context-aware crosswalk mappings that support long-term compliance and audit readiness. Or use NIST’s or SCF’s crosswalk mapping directly if it already satisfies your need.

results.title: Appendix — Dataverse.org
results.content: ## Metadata References. The Dataverse Project is committed to using standard-compliant metadata to ensure that a Dataverse installation’s metadata can be mapped easily to standard metadata schemas and be exported into JSON format (XML for tabular file metadata) for preservation and interoperability. ### Supported Metadata. Detailed below are what metadata schemas we support for Citation and Domain Specific Metadata in the Dataverse Project:. * Citation Metadata (see .tsv): compliant with DDI Lite, DDI 2.5 Codebook, DataCite 4.5, and Dublin Core’s DCMI Metadata Terms . * Geospatial Metadata (see .tsv): compliant with DDI Lite, DDI 2.5 Codebook, DataCite 4.5, and Dublin Core. * Social Science & Humanities Metadata (see .tsv): compliant with DDI Lite, DDI 2.5 Codebook, and Dublin Core. * Astronomy and Astrophysics Metadata (see .tsv): These metadata elements can be mapped/exported to the International Virtual Observatory Alliance’s (IVOA) VOResource Schema format and is based on Virtual Observatory (VO) Discovery and Provenance Metadata. * Life Sciences Metadata (see .tsv): based on ISA-Tab Specification, along with controlled vocabulary from subsets of the OBI Ontology and the NCBI Taxonomy for Organisms. * Journal Metadata (see .tsv): based on the Journal Archiving and Interchange Tag Set, version 1.2. * 3D Objects Metadata (see .tsv). ### Experimental Metadata. Unlike supported metadata, experimental metadata is not enabled by default in a new Dataverse installation. * CodeMeta Software Metadata: based on the CodeMeta Software Metadata Schema, version 2.0 (see .tsv version). * Computational Workflow Metadata (see .tsv): adapted from Bioschemas Computational Workflow Profile, version 1.0 and Codemeta. * Archival Metadata (see .tsv): Enables repositories to register metadata relating to the potential archiving of the dataset at a depositor archive, whether that be your own institutional archive or an external archive, i.e. a historical archive. * Local Contexts Metadata (see .tsv): Supports integration with the Local Contexts platform, enabling the use of Traditional Knowledge and Biocultural Labels, and Notices. Please note: these custom metadata schemas are not included in the Solr schema for indexing by default, you will need to add them as necessary for your custom metadata blocks. See also the Dataverse Software 4.0 Metadata Crosswalk: DDI, DataCite, DC, DCTerms, VO, ISA-Tab document and the Metadata Customization section of the Admin Guide.

results.title: Provenance Metadata Standards for Reliable Data
results.content: # Provenance Metadata Standards for Reliable Data ## Data Science Provenance Metadata This article discusses provenance metadata in data science, its applications, standards, and tools. Data provenance metadata describes its origins, modifications, and processes. Provenance metadata makes data history transparent, building trust. By documenting data’s path, changes, and procedures, provenance metadata allows data analysis to be reproduced. Data and model versioning helps capture provenance metadata. Versioning data and tracing its lineage helps capture provenance metadata. **E-commerce:** Tracking consumer and product data with provenance metadata improves trust and personalisation. **Complexity:** Tracking data transformations and procedures to capture provenance metadata is difficult and resource-intensive. Data science provenance metadata’s future consists in addressing difficulties and improving capabilities: Trustworthy and repeatable data science relies on provenance metadata.

Provides further background and resources to assist agencies in implementing the Project Open Data Metadata Schema v1.1. Project Open Data Metadata Schema,. This section provides further background and resources to assist agencies in implementing the Project Open Data Metadata Schema v1.1. In addition to template and sample files we also produce Project Open Data Metadata schema in JSON schema format. JSON schema describes a JSON data format. In order to then generate a data.json file from this, simply import the spreadsheet (in the form of a CSV file) into the CSV Converter, translate the metadata as needed, and then generate an appropriately formatted JSON file. CKAN is a popular, open-source data catalog that can be installed independently or run as a service. In addition to providing an effective means of organizing the agency’s data catalog, CKAN provides several opportunities for generating the needed data.json file. In addition to providing rich visualizations and data management features, Socrata **natively supports data.json** so any datasets managed through Socrata will be automatically exposed correctly. In order to generate appropriately formatted JSON, simply import an appropriately formatted CSV into the CSV Converter, ensure that the metadata fields line up, and re-export the file. Note the mapping for `license` and `rights` from Project Open Data to DCAT applies the fields from the Dataset object in Project Open Data to each of the Distribution objects in DCAT. FGDC member agencies developed these crosswalks as a standardized resource for use by agencies in creating their Project Open Data metadata schema v1.1 (data.json) records. The crosswalks are intended as a reference model for the development of strategies and applications that support the conversion of existing geospatial metadata to the Project Open Data metadata schema v1.1. You have been removed as maintainer of this record. #### GENERAL INFORMATION ### Research Metadata Schema Crosswalk Mappings to Schema.org The RDA Research Metadata Schemas Working Group has collected and aligned crosswalks from 15 source research metadata schemas to Schema.org. The source schemas include discipline agnostic schemas Dublin Core, Data Catalogue Vocabulary(DCAT), Data Catalogue Vocabulary - Application Profile (DCAT-AP), Registry Interchange Format - Collections and Services (RIF-CS), DataCite Schema, Dataverse; and discipline schemas ISO 19115-1, EOSC/EDMI, Data Tag Suite (DATS), Bioschemas, B2FIND, Data Documentation Initiative (DDI), European Clinical Research Infrastructure Network (ECRIN), Space Physics Archive Search and Extract (SPASE); as well as CodeMeta for software.
